Some memory chips used in Apple devices could be manufactured in the US for the first time, if plans involving one of the company's suppliers come to fruition.

A new report claims that Apple's memory supplier SK Hynix is in talks with Intel about the possibility of using a chip plant the latter is planning to build in Ohio...

Reuters reports that details remain unclear, but the South Korean company manufactures RAM and NAND flash memory chips for Apple devices.

Some processors used in Apple devices are already produced on US soil, but due to restrictions on foreign access to TSMC's most advanced processes, these processors can only be used in older models. No such restriction applies to DRAM or NAND flash memory chips, because Apple uses industry-standard versions.

However, the report notes that the plan could face opposition from the South Korean government, as South Korea may share Taiwan's concerns about exporting chip manufacturing technology, even for less advanced processes.

SK Hynix said nothing is finalized yet. Intel declined to comment on the report but confirmed it will continue to move forward with its Ohio plant plans.
